source_text: In the American Medical Association Journal of Ethics, contributors have asserted that proxy consent for non-therapeutic infant circumcision is ethically flawed, as it imposes iatrogenic injury—defined as harm from medical intervention without offsetting medical imperative—on a non-autonomous patient, advocating postponement to adulthood to respect bodily integrity. [4]
